title: S1096 (2025 Regular): Weapons and Firearms

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Florida); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Florida text (Introduced, 2025-02-25; official copy, https://www.flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2025/1096/BillText/Filed/HTML (LegiScan doc 3140007))

operative_text:
Section 2 (new s. 790.0653, F.S.): (2) All persons involved in firearm sales or other transfers, in whole or in part, are subject to background checks unless specifically exempted by state or federal law. A person may not sell or otherwise transfer a firearm unless: (a) The person is a licensed dealer; (b) The purchaser or other transferee is a licensed dealer; or (c) The requirements of subsection (3) are met. (3)(a) The seller or other transferor and the purchaser or other transferee shall appear jointly with the firearm at a licensed dealer and request that the licensed dealer conduct a background check on the purchaser or other transferee. (5) A person who violates this section commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.
Section 3 (s. 790.174, F.S.): (1)(b) A person who stores or leaves, on a premise under his or her control, a firearm as defined in s. 790.001, and who knows or reasonably should know that a prohibited user is likely to gain access to the firearm, shall keep the firearm in a securely locked box or container or shall secure it with a trigger lock, except when the person is carrying the firearm on his or her body or within such close proximity thereto that he or she can retrieve and use the firearm as easily and quickly as if he or she carried it on his or her body. (3) As used in this section, the term: (c) “Minor” means any person under the age of 18.
Section 4 (s. 790.175, F.S.): (1) Except as provided in subsection (2), a licensed dealer may not sell a firearm in this state unless the sale includes one of the following: (a) A commercially available trigger lock or other device designed to disable the firearm and prevent the discharge of the firearm. (b) A commercially available gun case or storage container that can be secured to prevent unauthorized access to the firearm.
Section 5 (new s. 790.223, F.S.): (2) It is unlawful to knowingly manufacture or assemble, cause to be manufactured or assembled, import, purchase, sell, offer for sale, or transfer ownership of any firearm that is not imprinted with a valid serial number. (4) Beginning January 1, 2026, it is unlawful to knowingly possess a firearm or any completed or unfinished frame or receiver that is not imprinted with a valid serial number. (5) A person may not knowingly manufacture or assemble or cause to be manufactured or assembled, import, sell, offer for sale, transfer, or possess any undetectable firearm. (6) It is unlawful to use a three-dimensional printer or computer numerical control (CNC) milling machine to manufacture or assemble any firearm or completed or unfinished frame or receiver within this state without a valid license to manufacture firearms.
